settings.heading: Learn the plant.
settings.text: I teach what's in your cup and where it came from. Not what it will do for you. Here's what I'd tell a friend who's curious.

settings.heading: What's in your cup
settings.intro: Ceremonial cacao is the whole bean ground into paste, so what the bean holds stays in. Here it is in plain words.

settings.title: Minerals
settings.text: Cacao contains magnesium, iron, copper, manganese, zinc, and potassium, minerals your body uses every day.

settings.title: Theobromine
settings.text: Cacao's main natural compound. It's a gentle stimulant in the same family as caffeine, and your body clears it more slowly than caffeine.

settings.title: A little caffeine
settings.text: Much less than a cup of coffee. The amount depends on the origin and how much you use.

settings.title: Flavanols
settings.text: Plant compounds called polyphenols, also found in tea and berries. Less processing leaves more of them in the bean.

settings.title: Cacao butter and fiber
settings.text: The bean's natural fat stays in the paste, which gives your cup its body. Cacao has fiber too.

settings.title: Nothing added
settings.text: No sugar, milk, or fillers. Just the bean.

settings.heading: How to make your cup
settings.intro: It takes about five minutes. A small whisk or frother helps.

settings.text: Shave or chop your cacao into small pieces.
Heat 6 to 8 oz of water or milk until steaming. Don't let it boil.
Whisk or blend until smooth and a little frothy.
Add cinnamon, vanilla, or a little honey if you like.

settings.heading: Find your amount
settings.intro: More isn't better. Most people need less than the internet says.

settings.title: A light sip
settings.text: A good first cup, and a good place to stay if you're sensitive to caffeine.

settings.title: A daily cup
settings.text: Where most people settle for a morning or afternoon cup.

settings.title: A gathering cup
settings.text: What I serve at guided gatherings. Check with your provider first if you have a heart condition or take medications.

settings.heading: Storing your block
settings.text:
Keep it sealed and airtight in a cool, dry place. Heat is the one thing that hurts it. A sealed block keeps one to two years.

If you see a white or dusty film, that's bloom. The cacao's own fat rose to the surface. It's not mold, and it's still good.
